insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'b170ab5a-f54f-4cae-ac2e-bd194181cafe', 'Text\nPart 6: Gapped Text
You are going to read an article about the importance of taking breaks while studying. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (31–36). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.

Text
Why Taking Breaks Improves Learning
Many students believe that studying for long hours without stopping is the best way to achieve good results. However, research suggests that taking regular breaks can actually improve learning.
(31) ______Short pauses during study sessions allow the brain to rest and process information more effectively.
Without breaks, it becomes harder to concentrate.(32) ______As a result, productivity often decreases over time.
Taking breaks can also help reduce stress.(33) ______Stepping away from work for a few minutes can improve your mood and energy levels.
Another benefit is that breaks can increase creativity.(34) ______When you return to your work, you may find new solutions to problems.
It is important, however, to use breaks wisely.(35) ______Activities such as checking social media can easily take longer than planned.
Instead, simple actions like stretching, walking or drinking water can be more effective.(36) ______These activities help refresh your mind without causing distractions.

Sentences
A This is because the brain needs time to recover.B After a while, people may start to feel tired and lose focus.C Choosing the right type of break is essential.D A short rest can prevent feelings of frustration.E Changing your activity can help you see things differently.F For this reason, many experts recommend studying in shorter sessions.G They allow you to relax without losing too much time.

Answer Key
31 F32 B33 D34 E35 C36 G
', now());

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of learning new skills. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions feeling more confident after learning something new?38 found it difficult to stay motivated at the beginning?39 learned something mainly for professional reasons?40 enjoyed the social aspect of the experience?41 talks about improving slowly over time?42 mentions being surprised by their own ability?

Texts
A – Laura
I decided to learn how to cook properly last year because I was tired of eating ready-made meals. At first, I found it quite challenging, especially because I made a lot of mistakes. However, I kept practising, and over time I noticed that my skills were improving little by little. Now I feel much more comfortable in the kitchen and even enjoy trying new recipes.

B – Mark
For me, learning graphic design was something I needed for my job. My company expected me to develop these skills, so I didn’t really have a choice. Although I wasn’t very interested at first, I soon realised that I was actually quite good at it. That surprised me, and now I even use these skills for personal projects.

C – Sofia
I joined a photography class because I wanted to meet new people while doing something creative. The classes were fun, and I really enjoyed sharing ideas with others. It was great to be part of a group where everyone supported each other. As a result, I not only improved my photography but also made several good friends.

D – James
I started learning a new language a few months ago. In the beginning, I found it hard to stay motivated because progress seemed very slow. Sometimes I felt like giving up, but I decided to continue. Eventually, I began to understand more, and that gave me the confidence to keep going.

Answer Key
37 D38 D39 B40 C41 A42 B
', now());

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of working from home. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions saving time because of their situation?38 found it difficult to separate work and personal life?39 prefers their current situation to their previous one?40 mentions feeling lonely at times?41 talks about becoming more productive?42 had no choice about the change?

Texts
A – Daniel
When my company decided that everyone had to work from home, I wasn’t very happy about it. I preferred going to the office, but there was nothing I could do. At first, it felt strange, but eventually I got used to it. Now I can see some advantages, although it wasn’t my decision to begin with.

B – Emma
Working from home has made a huge difference to my daily routine. I no longer spend hours travelling to work, which gives me more time to relax or exercise. I feel much happier now than I did before, and I wouldn’t want to go back to my old schedule.

C – Alex
At first, I thought working from home would be easy, but I quickly realised it wasn’t. I found it hard to stop working at the end of the day because everything happened in the same space. It was difficult to create clear boundaries between my job and my personal life.

D – Sara
One thing I didn’t expect was how much I would miss being around other people. Although I can communicate with my colleagues online, it’s not the same as seeing them in person. On the positive side, I’ve noticed that I can concentrate better and get more work done.

Answer Key
37 B38 C39 B40 D41 D42 A
', now());

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of practising sport regularly. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 says they didn’t enjoy the activity at the beginning?38 mentions that they needed encouragement to continue?39 talks about doing the activity for health reasons?40 says they have made new friends through the activity?41 mentions noticing gradual improvement?42 says they now feel more energetic?

Texts
A – Tom
I started running because my doctor advised me to be more active. At first, I didn’t really like it and found it quite tiring. However, I kept going because I knew it was good for my health. After a few weeks, I began to feel fitter and had much more energy during the day.

B – Lisa
Joining a local yoga class was one of the best decisions I’ve made. Not only have I become more flexible, but I’ve also met some great people. We often talk after class, and sometimes we even meet outside the sessions. It has become both a social and relaxing activity for me.

C – David
When I first started going to the gym, I found it difficult to stay motivated. There were days when I wanted to give up, but my friend encouraged me to keep going. Thanks to that support, I didn’t quit. Over time, I noticed small improvements, which helped me stay focused.

D – Anna
Swimming has always been something I enjoyed, but I never took it seriously until recently. Now I go to the pool three times a week. I’ve seen my technique improve gradually, and I feel more confident in the water. It’s satisfying to see progress, even if it’s slow.

Answer Key
37 A38 C39 A40 B41 D42 A
', now());

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nB2 First (FCE) – Reading and Use of English
Part 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of learning to play a musical instrument. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions that progress was slow but satisfying?38 says they started for practical reasons?39 found it difficult to practise regularly?40 enjoyed performing in front of others?41 mentions help from another person?42 was surprised by how much they improved?

Texts
A – Kevin
I decided to learn the guitar because I needed a hobby that would help me relax after work. At first, I didn’t practise as much as I should have, mainly because I was busy and often forgot. However, once I created a routine, I began to enjoy it more and improve steadily.

B – Marta
Learning the piano was not something I chose myself at the beginning. My parents wanted me to learn it when I was younger. Although I didn’t enjoy it much at first, I later realised how useful it was. I even performed at a school concert, which I found exciting.

C – Luis
When I started playing the violin, I found it quite difficult and progress was slow. However, each small improvement felt like an achievement. Over time, I became more confident and proud of what I could do.

D – Rachel
I began learning the drums with the help of a friend who already knew how to play. He showed me the basics and encouraged me when I felt stuck. I didn’t expect to improve so quickly, but after a few months I realised I had made much more progress than I thought.

Answer Key
37 C38 B39 A40 B41 D42 D
', now());

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of travelling alone. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions feeling nervous before starting?38 says the experience helped them become more independent?39 had a negative experience at some point?40 enjoyed having complete control over their plans?41 mentions meeting new people during the trip?42 says they would repeat the experience?

Texts
A – Julia
Before my first solo trip, I felt quite anxious because I had never travelled alone before. However, once I arrived, I realised I could manage everything by myself. By the end of the trip, I felt much more independent and confident in my abilities.

B – Carlos
Travelling alone gave me the freedom to decide exactly what I wanted to do each day. I didn’t have to compromise with anyone, which I really enjoyed. I could change my plans whenever I wanted, and that made the experience very relaxing.

C – Hannah
During my trip, I stayed in several hostels, which made it easy to meet other travellers. We shared stories, explored places together and even stayed in touch afterwards. It was one of the most social experiences I’ve ever had.

D – Liam
Although I generally enjoyed travelling alone, there was one moment when I got lost in an unfamiliar city and felt quite stressed. Despite that, I learned a lot from the experience, and I would definitely consider doing it again in the future.

Answer Key
37 A38 A39 D40 B41 C42 D
